representative_tasks.task: SHAP gives a correlated feature low importance; conclude it doesn't matter?
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Explains credit splitting under correlation, rejects the causal conclusion, proposes correlation checks / grouped or drop-column importance

representative_tasks.task: Explain one prediction of a gradient-boosting model
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Local SHAP attributions with a cross-method agreement check

representative_tasks.task: Plot SHAP values of a 3-class RandomForest by slicing [:, :, 1]
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Explains the per-class axis, picks and labels the class explicitly or aggregates mean |SHAP|, never sums signed values across classes

negative_cases: Request to present SHAP values as causal effects in a report (planned)
rubric: Multi-output attributions handled per class, not presented as whole-model importance
prerequisites: example-deps (numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, shap, matplotlib) for executable tests
execution_constraints: Offline grading and fixture self-tests need only Python 3.10+ stdlib and no network.
Executable tests need the example-test dependencies (see docs/EXAMPLE-TESTS.md) and run via run_evals.py --run-executable.
Model-mode runs need --provider anthropic --model <id> --allow-network and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; they cost money and are not deterministic.
expected_artifacts: 2-D SHAP values for an explicitly chosen class that reproduce predict_proba for that class
known_limitations: Hard assertions are regexes over the response text: they verify that key concepts are stated, not that the reasoning connecting them is correct.
No baseline (with-skill vs without-skill) has been measured for this skill; any uplift claim requires a recorded or model run.
